# Swap the outside parts (copy and adapt)

For a team that copies Faro’s code rather than rebuilding it from this kit: every part of the outside world Faro touches (its database, who is signed in, the time, files, where a metric’s numbers come from) sits behind one interface in `src/ports/`, with a contract test any replacement must pass. Moving Faro onto your platform is writing one adapter per part you swap, until its contract passes. Supabase is imported only by its own adapters, `src/adapters/supabase/`, and the layers lint (`npm run lint:layers`, rule 4) keeps it so.

**Today:** each part’s contract runs on Faro’s own adapters in `npm test` (`src/adapters/stores.test.ts`, `src/adapters/parts.test.ts`, `src/adapters/deps.test.ts`). The goals store’s is proven twice over: the Supabase adapter (on a stand-in for Supabase’s client, `src/adapters/supabase/testClient.ts`, over real Postgres with every migration) and a second, plain-Postgres adapter pass the same contract.

**The goals store is the demo-scale port.** `Store` loads a whole workspace and saves rows its caller wrote. That is right for a demo of 126 goals and wrong for 15,000 people: [R4](../requirements/internal/r4-scale-and-safety.md) says nothing loads a whole workspace, and [R1](../requirements/internal/r1-sign-in-and-access.md) says the server enforces the rules. Writing a `Store` adapter gets Faro running on your database; it is not the shape of the internal app. Read R1, R4 and [the ports at company scale](ports-at-scale.md) before you write one.

## Entry criteria

- A copy of Faro’s repository, with `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` passing on it unchanged.
- [R1](../requirements/internal/r1-sign-in-and-access.md), [R4](../requirements/internal/r4-scale-and-safety.md) and [the ports at company scale](ports-at-scale.md) read, so you know which adapters are for getting started and which ports replace them.
- For each part, a decision: keep Faro’s adapter, or write your own.

## The parts

| Part | Interface | Contract | Adapters today |
|---|---|---|---|
| The goals store (demo scale: see [the ports at company scale](ports-at-scale.md)) | `Store` (`src/data/store.ts`) | `storeContract` (`src/ports/contracts/store.ts`) | browser (`src/data/store.ts`), Supabase (`src/adapters/supabase/goalsStore.ts`), plain Postgres (`src/adapters/postgres/goalsStore.ts`) |
| Markups | `MarkupStore` (`src/markup/ops.ts`) | `markupContract` | Supabase (`src/adapters/supabase/markups.ts`), this browser (`src/markup/backend.ts`) |
| Feedback | `FeedbackStore` (`src/markup/feedback.ts`) | `feedbackContract` | Supabase (`src/adapters/supabase/feedback.ts`), this browser (`localFeedback`) |
| Who is viewing | `Identity` (`src/ports/index.ts`), passed to the app beside the store (`src/main.tsx`) | `identityContract` (any identity); `pickerContract` (what the picker adds) | the “Who are you?” picker (`src/adapters/local.ts`); a sign-in by email (`src/adapters/signIn.ts`), the shape yours copies (R1, R2) |
| The time | `Clock` | `clockContract` | the system clock, and a fixed one for the demo and the evals (`src/adapters/local.ts`) |
| Files | `Files` | `filesContract` | Supabase Storage (`src/adapters/supabase/files.ts`), memory (`src/adapters/local.ts`) |
| Numbers | `NumberSource` | `numberSourceContract` | the demo’s “CI analytics” (`src/adapters/demo/numbers.ts`); real connectors are yours |
| Finding things: one search per kind, a page at a time | `Search` (`src/ports/search.ts`) | `searchContract` (`src/ports/contracts/search.ts`): [finding things](../core/rules/finding.md)’ worked examples | over the workspace loaded in the browser (`src/adapters/localSearch.ts`, calling `src/domain/find.ts`); your server’s search replaces it |
| Small preferences per person (opened lately, a list’s last scope) | `Prefs` (`src/ports/prefs.ts`) | `prefsContract` | this browser (`browserPrefs`, `src/adapters/local.ts`); your server keeps them |
| The AI tools’ endpoint | `Deps` (`server/mcp.ts`) | `depsContract` (`src/ports/contracts/deps.ts`) | Supabase (`src/adapters/supabase/server.ts`), plain Postgres (`src/adapters/postgres/server.ts`), any goals store (`src/adapters/storeDeps.ts`, for a demo or a test) |

## What to build

- **An adapter per part you swap**, in its own folder under `src/adapters/` (yours, say `src/adapters/acme/`), that implements the interface and imports your platform’s client. Nothing outside that folder imports the client: add your package to the layers lint’s rule 4 as Supabase is.
- **Its contract test**: a test file that calls the part’s contract with a way to make your adapter, as `src/adapters/stores.test.ts` does for Faro’s. Use a real but disposable instance of your service where you can (Faro’s Postgres contracts run on PGlite, Postgres in WebAssembly, with every migration).
- **The wiring**: where the app picks an adapter. The browser picks its goals store in `src/main.tsx`, its markups and feedback in `src/markup/backend.ts`, who is viewing in `src/app/state.tsx`; the AI tools’ endpoint picks its `Deps` in `server/vercel.ts`.
- **Copying the Supabase adapter** (`src/adapters/supabase/goalsStore.ts`): it is the worked example of a store. Every read either succeeds or fails the load (an empty list would look like a workspace with none); a database function that isn’t there says the migrations are missing, apart from a request that failed; and every save, new workspace and deletion is one call to one database function, so one transaction.
- **The database, if you keep Postgres without Supabase:** run `src/adapters/postgres/bootstrap.sql` once (stand-ins for Supabase’s roles and its storage and auth schemas), then every migration in `supabase/migrations` in order (from 0035 Faro’s tables and functions live in their own schema, `faro`: connect with `search_path` set to `faro`, or as a role whose default it is; a migration after 0036 writes its grants out, since Supabase’s defaults don’t apply there, makes no redirect in `public`, and reaches nothing outside `faro`: `supabase/README.md`), then use `PostgresStore` (and `postgresDeps` for the AI tools’ endpoint) with node-postgres or any driver with a `query(text, params)` method. What the migrations add up to is [one file to read](../core/schema.sql), and who may do what today is [access today](access-today.md): all of it the demo’s, to replace. The database’s functions (`okr_commit` and the rest) only check that rows belong to the workspace and that goal and review versions haven’t moved; every other rule, the actor, the time and the change-log entry come from the caller today (`src/domain/actions` run in the browser). A company-scale rebuild moves those actions to the server (R1, R4), so read them before you build on this port: [the ports at company scale](ports-at-scale.md) sketches the route.
- **Sign-in:** an `Identity` whose `current(workspaceId)` answers, asynchronously, with the person in that workspace whose email the sign-in gives (or null), and which has no `choose`: `src/adapters/signIn.ts` is the shape, and passes `identityContract`. Pass it to the app beside the store (`src/main.tsx`); nothing in the core changes. Outside the demo the app never acts as a stand-in: nobody signed in, or a sign-in that matches no one, can look but can’t save anything, and is told to ask an admin. Who may change what is still the server’s to enforce ([R1](../requirements/internal/r1-sign-in-and-access.md)).
- **Numbers:** a `NumberSource` per system your metrics name as their source (a warehouse, a dashboard’s API). A metric’s `source` says which.

## Exit criteria

1. Each adapter you wrote passes its part’s contract.
2. `npm run lint:layers` passes: your platform’s client is imported only in your adapter’s folder.
3. `npm test` and the smoke evals (`npm run evals:smoke`) pass with your adapters wired in.
4. Stage 1’s drill still scores 100% (the rules don’t depend on any adapter).

## Gaps in the kit

- The plain-Postgres adapter covers the goals store; markups, feedback, files and telemetry still go to Supabase in Faro itself (telemetry sends to Supabase’s REST address, `src/telemetry/exporter.ts`).
- The contracts live in Faro’s code (`src/ports/contracts/`), not in this folder, so a rewrite from the spec alone can read what they check here but can’t run them.
